positioning: vLLM v0.27.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

# What's New in vLLM v0.27.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.27.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
